      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers</link>
      <description><p>Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner</p><p>The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/23/unemployment-to-surpass-5-and-things-will-get-a-bit-harder-treasurer-jim-chalmers-warns</link>
      <description><p>Economists flag rising recession risk as government forecasts economy will grow by less than 2% in 2027 and 2028</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/23/anthony-albanese-digital-duty-of-care-labor-greens-coalition-one-nation-angus-taylor-pauline-hanson-penny-wong-ai-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Jim Chalmers has warned Australians that “things will get a bit harder before they get easier”, revealing next month’s budget update will show unemployment climbing above 5% alongside slower economic growth for the next two years.</p><p>As economists flagged rising recessionary risks, the treasurer used a ministerial statement during question time to reveal what he described as “concerning” economic numbers in the upcoming mid-year economic and fiscal outlook.</p><p><strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/aug/28/politics-really-newsletter-guardian-australia-free-best-daily-auspol-email-subscribe?CMP=copyembed">Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here</a></strong></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/23/unemployment-to-surpass-5-and-things-will-get-a-bit-harder-treasurer-jim-chalmers-warns">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions</p><p>Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.</p><p>That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.</p><p><em><strong>Cop</strong></em><em><strong>31 </strong></em>| The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected">rejected what they called an unacceptable deal</a> that “failed to meet the moment” in a dramatic finish to the UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal failed to endorse a away from fossil fuels that more than 130 countries demanded.</p><p><em><strong>Russia </strong></em>| A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in a suspected <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Ukrainian sea drone attack</a>, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p><em><strong>Weapons</strong></em>| The Red Cross and other rights groups <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/22/red-cross-warns-too-late-regulate-autonomous-weapons-united-nations">have warned that it will soon</a> be too late to properly regulate the development of autonomous weapons. The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/22/nhs-savings-hospitals-trusts-england-cuts"> the Guardian can reveal.</a></p><p><em><strong>West Bank </strong></em>| Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/netanyahu-rival-condemns-settler-arson-attacks-palestinian-villages-west-bank">condemned arson attacks</a> by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank after dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday.</p><p><em><strong>Monday</strong></em> | FIFA is set to announce that the UK will host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday </strong></em>| RMT will begin a series of eight 24-hour strikes on the London Underground over the next three months due to a dispute over a four-day week for its drivers.</p><p><em><strong>Sunday</strong></em> | Spain will hold snap parliamentary elections in what will be the country’s sixth general election in 11 years.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Burnham not ‘backtracking’ on creating closer links with EU, officials say</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-not-backtracking-creating-closer-links-eu-officials-say</link>
      <description><p>Government wants to let trade deal ‘breathe a bit’, insiders say, after speculation No 10 is dialling back ambitions</p><p>Andy Burnham is not backtracking or delaying his ambitions to create even closer links with the EU in the wake of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/20/burnham-trade-youth-mobility-deals-biggest-step-towards-eu-since-brexit">a landmark summit</a> in Brussels, the Guardian has been told, after signs of an apparent slowdown in the timetable.</p><p>The prime minister has promised to set out options for the UK’s long-term relationship with the EU, including the possibility of rejoining, saying last week that these would be outlined later in the year.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-not-backtracking-creating-closer-links-eu-officials-say">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend</link>
      <description><p>Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday</p><p>Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2026/nov/19/trump-greets-putin-before-holding-talks-at-apec-summit-video">their recent meeting</a> in China.</p><p>Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and <a href="https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117656427563362319">posted a photo of himself and Putin </a>shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected</link>
      <description><p>EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels</p><p>The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey.</p><p>The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 06:48:49 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec3acb0c-e4dd-11f1-9619-3935a39ed096</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:24:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-france-probes-suspected-leaks-from-interior-ministry-to-far-right-national-rally</link><description>
France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5be0a25a-e4b2-11f1-be46-714476ef8919</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French union leader warns strikes will continue without higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-union-leader-warns-strikes-will-continue-without-higher-wages-cgt-sophie-binet-interview</link><description>
French trade unions have promised to call more strikes and demonstrations, arguing that a government proposal to increase the minimum wage fails to address the social crisis that has spurred protests across the country. Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, says even after six weeks of action, workers and students are more determined than ever to keep up the fight.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37c8b342-e40f-11f1-a821-bd0c1d2fd9c6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:07:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© REUTERS - Sarah Meyssonnier </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da07160a-e41c-11f1-9424-dd481487d627</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:19:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261119-france-raises-bird-flu-alert-to-highest-level-as-infections-spread-across-europe</link><description>
France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eff2afda-e3f7-11f1-a0c0-bdb47d3d53b3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:12:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png">© GAIZKA IROZ / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. Although turnout was lower than at previous protests, anger remained strong – with many demonstrators also voicing fears about the far right coming to power in the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b33b0b8-e32a-11f1-9717-657339b41114</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:50:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-eu-economics-chief-warns-france-and-belgium-must-reduce-deficit-and-public-debt</link><description>
France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">065f0570-e281-11f1-84fb-2734eec1674a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:00:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-a-message-to-drug-gangs-life-sentences-for-barbaric-marseille-murders</link><description>
Two leading figures in Marseille's drug-trafficking underworld were sentenced to life imprisonment on Monday for a triple murder in 2020. Anti-drugs activist Amine Kessaci, whose brother was among the victims, hailed the verdict as a "message to the narcocracy".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1288fd3c-e282-11f1-91a0-f16e280f34ca</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:59:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg">AFP - THIBAUD MORITZ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French presidential candidates clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-french-presidential-candidates-clash-over-tax-housing-and-the-minimum-wage</link><description>
Five candidates for the 2027 French presidential election on Monday evening wrangled over issues including the cost of living crisis, the minimum wage and single parents in a live televised debate. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">20e86fa6-e26a-11f1-8eb4-bd86e9020d76</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:50:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg">via REUTERS - KENZO TRIBOUILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Le Pen to end France’s financial aid to Ukraine if elected president</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-le-pen-to-end-france-s-financial-aid-to-ukraine-if-elected-president</link><description>
Marine Le Pen on Monday said that France would provide no further financial aid to Ukraine if she is elected president next year, after a meeting with Kyiv's ambassador in Paris.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2a8883b2-e278-11f1-aabb-77a008c9523d</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:50:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuentes / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second nationwide strike over demands for higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-france-braces-for-second-nationwide-strike-over-demands-for-higher-wages</link><description>
France is braced for its second nationwide strike in less than a fortnight on Tuesday, after unions called on nearly six million public-sector workers to take to the streets to demand higher wages.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">678bf058-e266-11f1-92d6-39b0dbf095fa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French actor Depardieu withdraws appeal against conviction for sexual assault</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-actor-depardieu-withdraws-appeal-against-conviction-for-sexual-assault</link><description>
French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>
Five families of Harkis – Algerians who fought for the French during Algeria's war of independence – have filed a legal complaint seeking answers over children who died in the 1960s in a former Harki camp in the south of France, and whose remains have since disappeared.

Thousands of women in France have reported unusually painful periods, heavy bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after being exposed to tear gas during the country's recent protests, prompting calls for an investigation into its possible effects on reproductive health.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/who-are-anthropic-founders">Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?</a></p></li></ul><p>As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it.       <description><p>Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights</p><p>More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an<a href="https://uniglobalunion.org/wp-content/uploads/Amazon-procurement-letter-embargoed-until-nov-19.pdf"> open letter</a> published on Thursday.</p><p>“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house.       <description><p>A citizen referendum, only the second of its kind in Georgia history, seeks to block a zoning amendment</p><p>Ire Gene Grovner stood behind his house on a recent morning, between chicken pens on one side and rows of winter collard greens on the other, holding a knife and skinning a raccoon splayed across a wood post.</p><p>“The meat is good roasted,” Grovner said.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.</p><p>Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/brighton-rocking-premier-league-elite-title-challenge">the headline-grabbing moments</a>, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit</p><p>There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/championship-roundup-southampton-birmingham-middlesbrough-swansea">second in the Championship table</a> and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.</p><p>Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mark-robins-stoke-birmingham-championship-premier-league-promotion">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england</link>
      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor &amp; Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview</link>
      <description><p>Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham</p><p>The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.</p><p>Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 19:20:51 GMT</pubDate>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/0671343c3cf539d0fa4d9b7314a9e14107aec25a/222_0_2220_1776/master/2220.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=d5fca600a6a968fab47427a472303557">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/Getty Images</media:credit>
      </media:content>
      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/0671343c3cf539d0fa4d9b7314a9e14107aec25a/222_0_2220_1776/master/2220.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=0d7ffe7c22389cfb3302579b9c858440">

    <item>
      <title>Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>For <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/aston-villa">Aston Villa</a>, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.</p><p>Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title><![CDATA[France 24 - Infos, news & actualités - L'information internationale en direct]]></title><description>France 24 décrypte l’actualité internationale, politique, l’économie, l’environnement, la culture, le sport, en France et à l’international avec analyses, des interviews, des reportages exclusifs, des magazines et des documentaires.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:57:11 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Sports</category><title>Ligue 1 : renversé par Le Mans, Marseille rechute après 5 victoires consécutives</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/sports/20261123-ligue-1-renvers%C3%A9-par-le-mans-marseille-rechute-apr%C3%A8s-5-victoires-cons%C3%A9cutives</link><description>
L’Olympique de Marseille s’est incliné à domicile face au Mans (3-2). Alors qu’il menait 2-0 après 40 minutes et des buts de Gouiri (33’) et Paixão (40’), l’OM s’est écroulé.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659a3e8c-e6e2-11f1-a088-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/om-1-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659a3e8c-e6e2-11f1-a088-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/om-1-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8b865d4c-e6e2-11f1-a878-2fb0ef8e8037</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:30:26 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>L'Equipe TV</dc:creator></item><item><category>Dans la presse</category><title>COP31, le flop</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/dans-la-presse/20261123-cop31-le-flop</link><description>
A la une de la presse, ce lundi 23 novembre, l’échec de la COP31, à cause, notamment, de référence aux énergies fossiles, dans la proposition finale. Le choc, en Italie, après le suicide d’un ancien chef de la police, retrouvé mort, samedi, à son domicile. Les témoignages des sœurs de Pengo Bossio Wangi, victime d’un assassinat raciste à Trappes, en banlieue parisienne, il y a un mois jour pour jour. Et une découverte qui va peut-être nous éclairer un peu plus sur nos origines.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a9c87c0-e70d-11f1-b28d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/1-METRO-COP.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a9c87c0-e70d-11f1-b28d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/1-METRO-COP.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a5e4866a-e70e-11f1-92e4-35b4a6e1a182</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:22:31 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Hélène FRADE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Ukraine en direct : Zelensky revendique des frappes contre deux navires russes en Libye</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/europe/20261123-ukraine-en-direct-au-moins-15-morts-dans-des-frappes-russes-pr%C3%A8s-de-kiev</link><description>
Le président ukrainien Volodimir ‌Zelensky a revendiqué des frappes contre deux navires russes au large des côtes libyennes dimanche. Au moins 15 personnes ont été tuées dans des frappes russes dans la région de Kiev, dont 11 dans l'effondrement partiel d'un immeuble résidentiel, selon le dernier bilan des autorités lundi. Une réunion de l'Otan est prévue lundi à Bruxelles au sujet du conflit. Suivez notre direct.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/236d35e6-e6a1-11f1-a665-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649708436.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/236d35e6-e6a1-11f1-a665-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649708436.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">612bdb50-e703-11f1-b5a9-3515bb9716c9</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 06:01:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/236d35e6-e6a1-11f1-a665-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649708436.jpg">© AP via Vantor satellite image</source><dc:creator>David RICH</dc:creator></item><item><category>Moyen-Orient</category><title>Israël : les partis d'Eisenkot et de Netanyahu achèvent leurs discussions sans parvenir à un accord</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/moyen-orient/20261123-israel-partis-gadi-eisenkot-benjamin-netanyahu-achevent-discussions-sans-parvenir-accord-likoud-coalition</link><description>
Une semaine après une première rencontre, les partis de Benjamin Netanyahu (Likoud) et de Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) ont conclu dimanche de nouveaux pourparlers en Israël. Ils ne sont pas parvenus à trouver un accord sur une éventuelle coalition. Une nouvelle réunion a été annoncée.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3264e3e-dd4f-11f1-a6a1-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314586138425.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3264e3e-dd4f-11f1-a6a1-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314586138425.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9abbebf6-e6fb-11f1-8f97-0115e6cbaf3a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 05:19:28 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3264e3e-dd4f-11f1-a6a1-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314586138425.jpg">© Ohad Zwigenberg, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Turquie : la COP31 se termine, sans accord</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-turquie-la-cop31-se-termine-sans-accord</link><description>
Malgré deux semaines de négociations, aucun consensus n'a pu être trouvé au terme de la COP31 à Antalya. L'UE a refusé un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles. "Nous n'approuverons pas une décision (...) ne mentionnant même pas les combustibles fossiles, qui sont le principal moteur du changement climatique", a annoncé le ministre irlandais du Climat, Darragh O'Brien. D'autres pays comme le Panama, les îles Marshall, le Vanuatu ou Belize ont affiché la même détermination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d0f71f18-e6f8-11f1-9242-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-040313-040511-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d0f71f18-e6f8-11f1-9242-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-040313-040511-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d5f4ea18-e6f8-11f1-9f77-6df6dcc2d776</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 04:48:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Double attaque contre des bateaux au large de la Libye</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-double-attaque-contre-des-bateaux-au-large-de-la-libye</link><description>
Sur des images publiées sur les réseaux sociaux, on peut apercevoir une corvette russe en feu. Plus tard, un navire marchand, dont le pavillon n'a pas été précisé, a été pris pour cible au large de la ville de Benghazi. Après ces deux attaques de navire, l'État major de la marine a voulu rassurer le peuple libyen, rappelant disposer des moyens nécessaires pour faire face à ce type de menaces.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a5594710-e6f7-11f1-8195-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-040123-040250-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a5594710-e6f7-11f1-8195-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261123-040123-040250-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">aae7f3b6-e6f7-11f1-ba9b-3f8d2537ce8e</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 04:44:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Afrique</category><title>Mali : Amnesty va lancer une campagne pour exiger la libération de l'influenceuse Rokiatou Doumbia</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20261123-amnesty-international-lance-campagne-liberation-influenceuse-rokiatou-doumbia-mali-junte-prison-association-malfaiteurs</link><description>
Amnesty se mobilise pour l'influenceuse Rokiatou Doumbia, alias "Rose, la vie chère", en lançant la campagne Écrire pour les droits pour réclamer sa libération. Voix critique de la junte, elle a été condamnée en août dernier à 10 ans de prison, dont trois avec sursis, pour "association de malfaiteurs" et "atteinte au crédit de l'État".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/eea1cef6-e6f2-11f1-8d13-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/W4R-Banners-individual7-scaled-1468x710.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/eea1cef6-e6f2-11f1-8d13-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/W4R-Banners-individual7-scaled-1468x710.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">47ecf39e-e6f0-11f1-bbc9-ddff91b5a481</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 04:05:23 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/eea1cef6-e6f2-11f1-8d13-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/W4R-Banners-individual7-scaled-1468x710.jpg">© Amnesty international</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : "La dynamique de vote utile s'exprime de manière très anticipée"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-2027-la-dynamique-de-vote-utile-s-exprime-de-mani%C3%A8re-tr%C3%A8s-anticip%C3%A9e</link><description>
Au menu de Présidentielle 2027 : Jean-Luc Mélenchon continue de rallier à gauche, Dominique de Villepin et David Lisnard bousculent le jeu à droite, et le RN fragilisé par les affaires.  Avec Frédéric Micheau, Directeur général adjoint de l'institut de sondages OpinionWay, et Richard Werly, éditorialiste politique et journaliste pour le media suisse en ligne Blick. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b07c4258-e6c7-11f1-affe-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-22T20-09-25-784Z.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b07c4258-e6c7-11f1-affe-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/Francais-2026-11-22T20-09-25-784Z.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">27cc6814-e6bf-11f1-9ce7-3f3625b48cf9</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 22:54:49 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Elections générales en RD Congo, la Symocel doute de la possibilité de tenir les délais</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261122-elections-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rales-en-rd-congo-la-symocel-doute-de-la-possibilit%C3%A9-de-tenir-les-d%C3%A9lais</link><description>
En RD Congo, se dirige-t-on vers un report des élections générales ? Les scrutins sont prévus en décembre 2028. Dans un rapport publié en novembre, la Symocel, l’une des missions d’observation électorale, doute de la possibilité de tenir ce délai...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e8ac38-e6bc-11f1-b05d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/WB299310-O-01-20261122-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e8ac38-e6bc-11f1-b05d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/WB299310-O-01-20261122-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">af117e7e-e6bd-11f1-b884-73184c4a7611</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:42:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Kalidou SY</dc:creator></item><item><category>Afrique</category><title>Libye : deux navires attaqués par des drones maritimes, dont un bateau russe</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20261122-libye-drones-maritimes-attaqu%C3%A9-deux-navires-bateau-russe-guerre</link><description>
Un incendie s'est déclaré dimanche après une explosion à bord d'un navire russe dans la base navale de Benghazi, en Libye. Le ministère de la Santé des autorités de l'Est a indiqué que le bateau avait été "ciblé par des drones maritimes". Dans la soirée, un deuxième bateau, dont le pavillon n'a pas été communiqué, a été attaqué dans le même port. La mission de l'ONU en Libye réclame une enquête indépendante.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8156d5f6-e6b8-11f1-a6fb-6fc2f3d2d784</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:05:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg">© AP via Vanto satellite image</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Philippe Sands : "l'arrêt de la CIJ fait partie des moments-clés qui changent l'Histoire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-philippe-sands-l-arr%C3%AAt-de-la-cij-fait-partie-des-moments-cl%C3%A9s-qui-changent-l-histoire</link><description>
La Cour Internationale de Justice a reconnu un génocide commis par la Birmanie à l'encontre de la minorité musulmane des Rohingya. La CIJ demande à ce que les réfugiés rohingya, pour la plupart entassés dans des camps au Bangladesh, puissent revenir en Birmanie et être indemnisés. L'avocat franco-britannique Philippe Sands, l'un des avocats qui ont représenté la Gambie contre la Birmanie devant la CIJ, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a96fd46c-e6b7-11f1-93d6-fb174a76721d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:59:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Caroline Toby : "sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-caroline-toby-sans-vid%C3%A9osurveillance-michel-zecler-aurait-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-victime-d-une-erreur-judiciaire</link><description>
Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences; or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtes à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-choose-france-entreprises-fran%C3%A7aises-pr%C3%AAtent-investir-42-5-milliards-euros-emmanuel-macron-%C3%A9conomie-investissements-projet</link><description>
Les entreprises tricolores projettent d'investir 42,5 milliards d'euros en France lors du sommet Choose France qui se déroulera lundi, a détaillé l'Élysée dimanche soir. Malgré une situation économique compliquée dans le pays, plus de 200 projets industriels français seront mis à l'honneur.
